extracted.intended_audience: NSERC Discovery Grants applicants and peer reviewers (Canadian research community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reviewer rubric for evaluating NSERC Discovery Grant applications (three equally-weighted criteria: Excellence of the Researcher; Merit of the Proposal; Contributions to HQP), including rating scale, bin matrix, and procedural requirements. Intended to be used by applicants preparing materials and by peer reviewers scoring applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the Researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three equally-weighted main criteria; assessed based on the researcher's contributions over the past 6 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed using multiple subcomponents (quality/impact of outputs, stature, knowledge, demonstrated expertise). Reviewers consider the influence of up to five nominated significant contributions; emphasis is on quality over quantity. The 6-year window standardizes career-stage evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and impact of contributions to research
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Excellence of the Researcher' covering publications and other outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes publications (quality > quantity), patents, software, technical reports, and other research outputs. Applicants should explain influence; reviewers weigh the impact and relevance of outputs rather than raw counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stature in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Excellence of the Researcher' assessing professional recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes invited talks, editorial roles, leadership positions and other indicators of recognition and leadership. Used to judge the researcher's standing and influence in the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Excellence of the Researcher' assessing current awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer checks that the applicant is up-to-date with the state of the art and aware of competing approaches. Demonstrated breadth and currency of knowledge increases the rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated expertise in the proposed research area
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Excellence of the Researcher' focusing on fit between researcher and proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence that the applicant has the relevant skills, prior work, or track-record to successfully carry out the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit of the Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three equally-weighted main criteria; assesses the scientific quality of the proposed research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated via subcomponents including originality/innovation, significance, clarity/scope of objectives, feasibility of approach, and how HQP training is integrated into the research. Reviewers consider the balance between ambitious aims and realistic plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Merit of the Proposal' assessing novelty of concepts or approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges whether the proposal advances knowledge with new ideas or methods. Innovation may include novel hypotheses, techniques, or interdisciplinary approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of the expected contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Merit of the Proposal' assessing importance of anticipated outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the potential impact of the work on the field, on applications, or on scientific understanding. Significance includes both immediate contributions and longer-term influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and scope of objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Merit of the Proposal' assessing how well aims are defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, well-scoped objectives that are logically organized and appropriately ambitious are rated higher. Overly vague or overly broad objectives are weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of the approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Merit of the Proposal' assessing methodological rigor and likelihood of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether methods, timelines, and resources make the objectives achievable. Feasibility includes consideration of risks, contingency plans, and methodological detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the training plan for HQP (as part of the proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcriterion under 'Merit of the Proposal' addressing how training of HQP is integrated into the research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for concrete plans for mentoring, skill development, and meaningful research experiences for students and trainees. The training plan here overlaps with the separate HQP criterion and is considered in both contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to the Training of Highly Qualified Personnel (HQP)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three equally-weighted main criteria; evaluates the applicant's record and plans for training HQP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly treated as a primary criterion. Reviewers assess the training environment, HQP achievements, and outcomes/skills gained by trainees. Strong HQP performance is required; a weakness here can veto funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcomponent of the HQP criterion covering the quality of laboratory, mentoring, and infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes availability of supervisory support, facilities, collaborations, and institutional resources that enable effective mentoring and research training.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQP awards and research contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcomponent of the HQP criterion focusing on trainees' measurable achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence includes students' awards, publications, fellowships, and other recognitions that signal successful training and student research contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and skills gained by HQP
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcomponent of the HQP criterion addressing career trajectories and transferable skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the employability, career progression, and transferable/technical skills trainees gain; long-term trainee outcomes strengthen the HQP rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-level descriptor rating scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Each main criterion is rated on a six-level scale: Exceptional (E), Outstanding (O), Very Strong (VS), Strong (S), Moderate (M), Insufficient (I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings are applied independently to each of the three criteria. The descriptors correspond to ordered qualitative judgments; reviewers must map evidence to these levels when scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard veto rule (Insufficient rating prohibits funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy rule: an 'Insufficient' (I) rating in any single criterion makes the application ineligible for funding regardless of other ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates asymmetry: excellence in other areas cannot compensate for an Insufficient in any one criterion. Reviewers should use 'Insufficient' only when the criterion is clearly lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal weighting of the three main criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring rule: 'Excellence of the Researcher', 'Merit of the Proposal', and 'Contributions to HQP' are equally weighted when combining ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSERC contrasts this with funders that emphasize researcher (e.g., ERC) or proposal (e.g., NIH) more heavily. Reviewers must treat all three as equally important inputs to the bin assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality bin matrix (A–J) for funding allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination rule: the three criterion ratings combine into a quality bin (A through J) that determines funding levels; e.g., Bin A = three Exceptional; Bin B = two Exceptional + one Outstanding; Bin J = three Strong (minimum fundable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSERC uses discrete funding bins rather than a continuous score; reviewers' descriptor-level choices drive bin placement. Bins lower than J are not funded. The document is explicit about several example bin combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6-year assessment window for past contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporal eligibility rule: Excellence of the Researcher is assessed using a 6-year retrospective window for significant contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standardizes evaluation across career stages; applicants nominate contributions from the prior 6 years. Extensions or accommodations (if any) should be addressed elsewhere in NSERC policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to list up to five most significant research contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Application-format requirement: applicants list up to five most significant research contributions from the last 6 years and explain their influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This caps the evidence reviewers will consider under 'Excellence of the Researcher' and emphasizes selecting and justifying the most influential outputs rather than exhaustive CV materials.
